assessment.intent: Show Okanagan and other small businesses how to turn one real customer project into useful website content, images, video, and social material without inventing proof or overclaiming results.
assessment.specificity: High. The article separates permission and briefing, project constraints, service-page versus case-study placement, video and social reuse, and the difference between one client-reported result and a general promise.
assessment.evidence: Good. It uses the approved Cool Runnings and ABC Appliance work conservatively, links the W3C accessibility guidance for video, and avoids unsupported percentages or invented customer quotes.
assessment.voice: Strong. It sounds like Michael: practical, answer-first, opinionated about judgement and restraint, conversational, and written for busy owners rather than marketers.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. The customer project worksheet, placement guidance, and clear limits around what one project can prove make this a reusable library article rather than thin portfolio advice.
